scope: Open review of superior sulcus (Pancoast) tumors: local invasion, the Pancoast-Tobias syndrome, and induction chemoradiotherapy before resection.

keyRecommendations.text: Induction chemoradiotherapy is the standard of care for a potentially resectable Pancoast tumor, followed by an attempt at complete resection.
The Pancoast-Tobias syndrome includes Horner syndrome, shoulder pain, hand and arm muscle atrophy, and subclavian vein obstruction.
Five-year survival after R0 resection is described as quite good (54 to 77 percent). Distant metastasis, especially brain, is the main recurrence pattern.

clinicalBottomLine: A Pancoast tumor invades the thoracic inlet and can cause the Pancoast-Tobias syndrome. For a potentially resectable tumor, give induction chemoradiotherapy and then try for a complete resection.
notableCaveats: Replaces the abstract-only PMC record with this open full review.

source.title: Superior sulcus (Pancoast) tumors: current evidence on diagnosis and radical treatment.
